claims.claim: A smart site is everything you need to know about a place, in one place.
Smart Site is the application that puts smart sites in your hands: map, layers, parcel answers, research, reports.
An Empressa product operated by Legacy Group ATX LLC.
source: public/privacy.html and public/terms.html already in production

claims.claim: The information that governs a property is scattered across the county GIS, the zoning ordinance, the FEMA panel, the code book; answering one real question means logging into all of them.
Smart Site assembles them against the place and answers the question with the source, the date and the confidence attached.
source: M01 We sell answers, not data
M08 Claims you may make freely

claims.claim: Map-first; no pages to navigate; every tool opens over the map; installs to a phone.
source: M05 First open and The map

claims.claim: The seven toggleable layers, verbatim in substance.
Presets Default, Flood, Entitlement, Terrain; measure, draw, marker, my location; search over parcels, addresses, streets, places with type-ahead and recents.
The parcel card carries land use, zoning district, setbacks, buildable envelope, flood status, acreage, and is free with no login.
Served from verified precomputed records rather than fetched and hoped; envelopes labelled approximate, not survey grade.
Where a fact is not verified the card says so, names what is missing, and never shows a guess.
One dock, one tool at a time, never a split screen, state remembered per property.
Property brief leads with a verdict line, red flags such as floodway placement lead when present, cited detail below.

Research is property-anchored; citations are numbered and tappable and open evidence, claim, source, confidence, date; the reasoning chain runs envelope to setback rule to code section; the assistant can only cite records that exist; several threads per property; attach documents; resume later.
source: M07 How do I know the AI isn't making things up

claims.claim: Saved properties hold brief, drawings, notes and research; Compare is side by side; a share link carries the analysis and lands the recipient on the live map at the property.
The report menu is X-ray, Flood and Drainage, Feasibility, Comparison.
Two generate today: the X-ray and the Flood and Drainage study, the latter a real computation with catchment, drainage zones, modeled ponding and traced flow lines.
source: M05 capability notes and Reports and exports

claims.claim: Feasibility and Comparison do not generate today; the Comparison side-by-side tool is live and the Comparison report is not.
Site plan export contents and terrain export formats.
Derived from public records, not a boundary survey, not for legal record, verify with city staff and licensed professionals.
source: M06 Not survey or legal work

claims.claim: Records is a request tool, not a report.
Coverage is nationwide United States, built jurisdiction by jurisdiction under mechanical certification gates, rolling out continuously.
We do not publish a county list, because a list is stale a month later and reads as a ceiling.
source: M06 must not enumerate specific counties as the extent of coverage or quote a dated count

claims.claim: Coverage is a question the product answers about your parcel, not a question you have to ask us.
source: M06 the 2026-08-10 replacement for the retired confirm-on-request line

claims.claim: Much unincorporated land is legitimately unzoned and an honest no-zoning-applies is the correct answer there.
source: M07 What happens where you don't have data

claims.claim: Citations open; confidence is labelled with its basis and says asserted where asserted; honest absence is styled distinctly; currency is checked and repealed or superseded records are caught; web-search context is labelled unverified.
source: M01 Currency is checked, not assumed

claims.claim: Two doors onto the same truth; the AI client calls mcp.smartsite.cloud; same facts, same citations, same confidence.

The connector is a door, not a plan: available at every rung including Free, signs in against the ordinary account, mirrors the workbench's gates, and nothing is moved onto or off it to make a rung attractive. It is not the Hauska catalog at mcp.hauska.dev.
source: D-CONNECTOR, which postdates M05 and M07 and rules exactly this

claims.claim: Browsing is anonymous; a free account adds saved properties, three research messages per property, and sharing; map, layers and the parcel card are free.
source: CODE: PE_FREE_CHAT_MESSAGE_LIMIT = 3 at artifacts/api-server/src/lib/peEntitlement.ts:21 — an independent second derivation that agrees with the master

claims.claim: The deep work sits behind a paid plan; the current plans and prices are in the app.
source: M06 Pricing, deliberately without the numbers; see deliberateOmissions

claims.claim: Sharing is free and a shared property carries everything the sharer stored at full fidelity regardless of the recipient's plan; what a plan gates is what you can produce, never what you can see of what was shared.
source: M06, the first of the three rulings that must survive translation

claims.claim: Not valuation.
source: M06 What Smart Site is deliberately not

claims.claim: No comps and no sold prices; Texas is a non-disclosure state so sale prices are not public record; the MLS vendor route is closed; sales history carries dates and events and marks the price absent.
source: D-MLS, What follows and stays true

claims.claim: Not a listings site.
Not survey or legal work; nothing approves, permits or certifies anything.
source: M08 Claims you may never make

claims.claim: There is no 3D or tilted view today and we do not promise one.

deliberateOmissions.omitted: Prices and the per-property unlock mechanic.
deliberateOmissions.why: The card forbids changing any pricing claim, the ladder is locked in a doc a static HTML file cannot track, and the in-app pricing surface is the source of truth. The page names the free layer in M06's own words and points at the app for the rest.

deliberateOmissions.omitted: M05's line that the site plan export collapses the one to three days an architect spends assembling a site base.
deliberateOmissions.why: M00, M01 and M08 forbid cycle-time, savings and ROI figures in market-facing material without exception. M05 carries the line as an internal walkthrough sentence; the ban is the stronger rule. Check 6 of the new guard now enforces it, so this omission is mechanical rather than remembered. This is a real tension INSIDE the master set and is routed rather than resolved here.

OPS-16 A-073 added P-109 the same day: export_instrument returns not_ready in production because HAUSKA_MCP_BASE_URL and HAUSKA_MCP_SERVICE_KEY are absent from the serving revision, while mcp.smartsite.cloud/llms.txt still advertises it. Publishing a tool list on a page nothing re-checks would republish that mismatch on a second surface.

deliberateOmissions.omitted: A Docs link in privacy.html's nav.
deliberateOmissions.why: privacy.html and terms.html carry identical navs. Adding Docs to one and not the other introduces a visible inconsistency, and terms.html is bounded off by card item 4. /docs is reachable by URL and links out to both legal pages; wiring it into the app chrome is named as leave-behind.

privacyRetentionProvenance.rule: Card item 1: every claim traced to a store, a job, or a code path. Full evidence in CP1 under storeFindingsThatGovernTheWords.

claims.claim: Removing a saved property deletes it along with the notes, research threads, chat summary, drawings and export record stored on it.
claims.traceTo: DELETE /property-explorer/v1/saved-properties/:parcelNodeId at artifacts/api-server/src/routes/propertyExplorer.ts:455 is a hard db.delete of the row. The row's snapshot jsonb is where that content lives: live key inventory over 23 production rows shows notes, chatThread, chatThreads, chatSummary, drawings, exports, sharePackages, shareReportSelection, status.

claims.claim: Removing a team member or an invitation deletes that row too.
Signing out clears the session cookie in your browser.
A share link stops resolving 30 days after it is created.
claims.traceTo: SHARE_TOKEN_TTL_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 in api/_lib/pe-share-token.ts, and api/_lib/pe-share-grant.ts refuses with share_grant_expired when Date.parse(row.expiresAt) has passed. Guard check 2 re-derives this on every CI run.

claims.claim: A signed-in session lasts 7 days.
claims.traceTo: SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 in api/_lib/session-cookie.ts, and independently DEFAULT_TTL_SEC = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 on the HMAC exp in artifacts/api-server/src/lib/sessionToken.ts. Two derivations, they agree.

claims.claim: Neither deletes anything; the share grant record remains after the link stops working.
claims.traceTo: No delete of peShareGrants exists anywhere in api-server routes or lib. Established by absence of a write path, NOT by data: production holds 12 grants, all expiring 2026-09-26 to 28, so no expired row has yet existed. The basis of the absence is named because an empty result is not an absence.

claims.claim: Everything else is kept for as long as the account exists, and no job deletes it on a schedule.
claims.traceTo: No pg_cron (pg_extension = plpgsql, postgis, vector). No triggers on any pe_* table, users, gtm_events or records_request_jobs (information_schema.triggers returns 0 rows). The only cron in .github/workflows is a Neon pooler connectivity canary. The four sweeps app.ts starts (briefing-generation-jobs, finding-runs, terrain-jobs, adapter-cache) were each read and none touches a pe_* table, gtm_events or records_request_*.

claims.claim: There is no delete-my-account button in the product today.
claims.traceTo: No self-serve deletion route under apps/property-explorer/api, and no delete-account affordance in src (searched for delete account, deleteAccount, close account, erase, right to be forgotten, data deletion). The only users delete is DELETE /users/:id at routes/users.ts:504 behind requireUsersManage, an admin console permission. The MCP surface has 13 tools and none deletes. Guard check 3 re-derives this on every CI run and fires in BOTH directions.

claims.claim: Removing the account record automatically removes, by a database constraint, sign-in identity, plan and Stripe reference, share grants, connected AI clients, chat counters and team membership.
claims.traceTo: information_schema referential_constraints on production: 12 FK rows reference users with delete_rule CASCADE, covering pe_user_identities, pe_user_entitlements, pe_share_grants, pe_ai_connections, pe_chat_message_counts, pe_team_members (both columns), pe_team_invitations, pe_workbench_state, pe_property_unlocks, pe_activation_events and user_auth_credentials.

claims.claim: It does not automatically remove your saved properties or your screens, which are keyed to your account but not linked by a constraint.
claims.traceTo: The FK query over pe_saved_properties, pe_screens and pe_screen_rows returns only pe_screen_rows -> pe_screens. Neither pe_saved_properties nor pe_screens has any FK to users. This is the single most important sentence on the page and it is the one a target-shaped policy would have got wrong.

claims.claim: The anonymous browse records carry no account link and cannot be matched back to you.
claims.traceTo: gtm_events.install_id is a random localStorage value from src/lib/installId.ts. gtm_events has no FK. peActivationEvents' own file header states the reason a separate account-scoped table was created: gtm_events is keyed on an install, and a signed-in funnel cannot be measured on it.

claims.claim: Before you sign in the app records that a browse started, which parcel you opened, and, when you search by address, the text you typed.
claims.traceTo: src/lib/gtmClient.ts event list; production payload keys on pe_browse_started (10,520 rows) are parcelNodeId and persona always, lookupSource on 4,916, lookupQuery on 241. Of those 241, 118 begin with a street number and 20 carry a state plus ZIP.

claims.claim: Files you attach stay in your browser; only the text your browser could read is sent.
claims.traceTo: src/workbench/tools/chat-attach.ts: the file lives client-side in thread session state, extracted text is injected into the outgoing message, there is no upload endpoint and no blob store.

claims.claim: We do not store card numbers; Stripe holds the payment method.
claims.traceTo: No column in the production schema matches card|pan|cvv|payment_method|iban|routing. pe_user_entitlements.stripe_customer_id is populated on 9 of 14 rows.

claims.claim: A transcript of your research chat is not written to our database.
claims.traceTo: artifacts/api-server/src/routes/brokerageBrief.ts /research/chat writes nothing but a GTM event, and only when an installId is present; the PE web path is the explicit no-installId branch. In production, 49 research_chat_turn events exist and ZERO carry a pe-* install id; their payload keys are messageLength, clientTier, areaScope, visibleParcelCount.

claims.claim: Composing an answer sends your question, the property records, and any attached text to a third-party AI model provider.
claims.traceTo: artifacts/api-server/src/lib/brokerageBriefLlm.ts resolves grok or anthropic with a rules-v1 fallback. The provider is deliberately not named on the page because it is resolved at runtime from configuration; naming one would be a claim that could be wrong on any given call.

claims.claim: Smart Site has no password of its own and never receives one.
claims.traceTo: user_auth_credentials belongs to the plan-review console (routes/auth.ts) and its intersection with pe_user_identities is ZERO by join. The equal count of 14 rows on each table is coincidence and was checked rather than assumed.

claims.claim: You sign in with Google or Microsoft, the app talks to those providers directly, and WorkOS handles one OAuth step when you connect an AI client.
claims.traceTo: apps/property-explorer/api/auth.ts: fetchIdTokenClaims for Google and fetchMicrosoftProfile for Microsoft, with PKCE. completeWorkOsExternalAuth runs only when pending.externalAuthId is set, which happens only via /api/auth/mcp-login?external_auth_id=. This CORRECTS the previous page text; see cp1 PRIV-1.

claims.claim: There is no revoke control in the product today; a link can be revoked on request.
claims.traceTo: Nothing under apps/property-explorer/src calls a share-grant revoke path (src/share only ever GETs /api/pe-share-grant). The revoke ROUTE exists at artifacts/api-server .../share-grants/:id/revoke and in the store interface, so the manual half of the sentence is true. Guard check 4 re-derives this on every CI run and fires in BOTH directions.

whatIAlmostGotWrong: The first run of the new guard FAILED on the real tree, and the failure was correct in form: the session sentence was right and split across two source lines. The tempting fix was to weaken the check to a keyword, which would have destroyed the meaning-shaped property. The fix taken was to normalise the input. Recorded because the weak fix is the one a hurried successor would reach for.

Check 6's patterns were run against all three pages BEFORE being wired in, and they fired on '100%' in every one. The source was calc(100% - 40px) in the inline CSS: normalizeProse stripped tags but not style bodies. Had I wired it in first and then adjusted the patterns to stop the noise, I would have narrowed a control to fit an artifact of my own extractor.

The synthetic fixture's non-privacy pages were four characters long, so check 6's positive control fired and the terms.html case never exercised check 6 at all. The guard caught its own test. Fixed by lengthening the fixture, not by lowering the floor.

The first violation battery reported REAL_EXIT wrong because $? was reading grep's status through a pipe, exactly DEV_PROCESS 2.3. Two of four cases read exit=0 while the guard had correctly exited 1. Re-run capturing node's own exit code before any of it was written down.
whatFailedAndStaysFailed: Card item 2's stated check is 'curl against the deployed host returns HTML rather than the shell'. This lane produces an uncommitted diff and does not deploy, so that check CANNOT be satisfied here and is not claimed. What is proven instead: the pre-state curl (/docs served 1,215 bytes of SPA shell, byte-identical in size to dist/index.html), the mechanism (a file in public/ plus a rewrite pair above the catch-all, the same one /privacy and /terms already use), the built artifact (vite copied dist/docs.html at 14,365 bytes), and a guard that fails if either half of the mechanism is removed. The deployed-host curl is owed after the planner commits and Vercel deploys, and is recorded as leave-behind with an owner.

wherePriorArtWasWrongAndIChangedIt.why: It asserted a value the page produced rather than one the source authority recognises, which ENFORCEMENT names directly: that converts a defect into a specification and makes the fix read as a regression. It did exactly that: correcting the sign-in sentence turned the suite red. Replaced with an assertion grounded in api/auth.ts, in both directions (WorkOS must still appear in its connector role; the wrong sentence must not).
wherePriorArtWasWrongAndIChangedIt.notChanged: The SAME assertion exists for terms.html on the next test, and terms.html still carries 'WorkOS AuthKit'. That file is bounded off by card item 4, so it was left alone and the finding is routed.
